chapter_note: This is a short, largely continuous cosmological instruction about the Living Spirit’s three ‘garments’ (wind, fire, water) and their spatial deployment across the zone. The only clear later material is the formulaic dialogue opening and direct address in ¶1; otherwise the chapter stays within cosmos→cosmos description without institutional or NT overlay.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.83⟩
that when the Living Spirit came he brought the three garments; that of wind, that of fire, and that of water. He assumed them from [ ... ] he has [ ... ] in them in those three garments [ ... ] he established [them] for all the things of [this univers]e, both above and below. He arranged them in the [ ... ] he was displayed. Afterwards [ ... ] his works [ ... ] the [ ... h]e stripped them off before [the ri]ghteous ones.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue/frame attribution and direct address: “Once again he speaks to his disciples:” and “Happen you know this, my beloved ones,” — late hagiographic/application voice wrapping a cosmological statement.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The paragraph begins with a formulaic speaking-scene plus second-person address (frame/application), then shifts into impersonal cosmological mechanics: the Living Spirit’s three garments (wind/fire/water) established ‘for all the things of this universe, both above and below’ and later ‘stripped… before the righteous ones’.

Now, when he was about to loose [n them, ... he] divested himself of them from their (clasp) and he [ ... i]n them, and thus these three g[arme]nts are arranged [ ... ] from below the edges of the zone as they clothe i[t al]l [ ... ] up [ ... ] above [ ... ] up [ ... ] above them strips them of the zone from that place at its topmost point; and it is placed below them and ra[ised u]p to the heights above, from which it had been sent o[u]t at their beginning.
